ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, D is a point on side AB, with $AD:DB = 3:4$ and $DE \parallel AC$, intersecting BC at point E. What is the value of $\frac{S_{\triangle BDE}}{S_{\triangle AEC}}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $DE\parallel AC$,\\
it follows that $\triangle BDE\sim \triangle BAC$, and $AD\colon DB=3\colon 4$,\\
thus $BD\colon AB=DE\colon AC=4\colon 7$, $S_{\triangle BDE}\colon S_{\triangle BAC}=16\colon 49$,\\
therefore $S_{\triangle BDE}\colon S_{\text{quadrilateral }DECA}=16\colon 33$,\\
since $DE\colon AC=4\colon 7$, and the heights of $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle ACE$ are equal,\\
it follows that $S_{\triangle ADE}\colon S_{\triangle ACE}=4\colon 7=12\colon 21$,\\
therefore $S_{\triangle BDE}\colon S_{\triangle AEC}=\boxed{16\colon 21}$.

Dividing the area ratios gives S_triangle_BDE/S_triangle_AEC = (16/49)/(21/49) = 16/21.
